/en/press/press-releases/ultra-high-perf.title: Continental Expands Portfolio of Large and High-Performance Tires

By the end of 2027, the company will add more than 650 new tire sizes across all tire lines, for both original equipment on new cars and the replacement market. By expanding its portfolio, the tire manufacturer is responding to growing demand for high-performance tires designed for larger, heavier and more powerful vehicles, as well as electrified drive systems, while laying the foundation for further profitable growth in this segment.

/en/press/press-releases/volkswagen-id-p.title: Fitted with Continental Tires: New Volkswagen ID. Polo

Adjusted free cash flow was also significantly higher than in the previous year. These improvements were driven primarily by a higher share of tires measuring 18 inches and above, continued positive effects from raw-material prices, lower impacts from exchange rates and tariffs as well as strict cost discipline.

/en/press/press-releases/20260506-q1-202.title: Continental Increases Profitability in Tires and ContiTech
/en/press/press-releases/20260506-q1-202.teaser: Continental started 2026 with a good first quarter. The Tires and ContiTech group sectors both increased their adjusted EBIT margins compared with the same quarter of last year, despite burdens from tariffs and exchange-rate effects. Adjusted free cash flow was also up year-on-year. By contrast, the economic environment and weak global markets hampered sales growth. Even against the backdrop of current geopolitical developments, the DAX-listed company has confirmed its full-year outlook. For 2026, Continental still expects consolidated sales of around €17.3 billion to €18.9 billion and an adjusted EBIT margin of around 11.0 to 12.5 percent.

/en/press/press-releases/20260430-superv.title: Sabrina Soussan Elected Chair of the Supervisory Board; Appointment of CEO Christian Kötz Extended
/en/press/press-releases/20260430-superv.teaser: Sabrina Soussan (56) has taken over as chair of the Supervisory Board of Continental AG. At its constituent meeting immediately following today’s Annual Shareholders’ Meeting, the Supervisory Board unanimously elected her as its chair. Shareholders had previously elected her to the Supervisory Board as a shareholder representative. Soussan succeeds Wolfgang Reitzle, who stepped down as planned at the end of today’s Annual Shareholders’ Meeting after serving on the Supervisory Board for more than 16 years.

/en/press/press-releases/20260430-annual.title: Continental Bids Farewell to Supervisory Board Chairman Wolfgang Reitzle
/en/press/press-releases/20260430-annual.teaser: At today’s Annual Shareholders’ Meeting in Hanover, Continental bid farewell to long-standing chairman of the Supervisory Board, Wolfgang Reitzle. As announced, Reitzle stepped down after 16 years at the helm of the Supervisory Board. “As chairman of the Supervisory Board, you have helped shape the company with determination and foresight. That requires not only the will to lead, but also courage. For that, you deserve our gratitude and respect,” said Sabrina Soussan, designated chair of the Supervisory Board. Continental CEO Christian Kötz also paid tribute to Reitzle’s achievements: “Without your personal dedication, Continental would not be where it is today. You have led us to the threshold of this new, exciting chapter. You provided crucial impetus for the clear strategic direction of our group sectors and for their independence.” At the same time, he added: “I am looking forward to working closely with Sabrina Soussan and to the next steps we will take together.”
